story_overview.title: The Yellow Wallpaper
story_overview.author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
story_overview.premise: A young wife, confined to an upstairs room for a rest cure, wants relief from her nervous condition, but her husband's well-meaning control and her own deteriorating mind resist. As she fixates on the room's wallpaper, the conflict resolves with her losing her grip on reality.
story_overview.concept: A woman undergoing a rest cure becomes obsessed with the yellow wallpaper in her room.

characters.name: The Narrator
characters.characterSketch: A young wife and new mother prescribed a rest cure for what her husband calls a temporary nervous depression.
characters.appearance: Pale and tired, kept in loose house clothes; rarely seen outside the room.
characters.physNotes: Fatigued, sleeps poorly, loses weight over the summer.
characters.psychNotes: Imaginative and observant; her perceptions are dismissed by those around her.
characters.flaw: Defers to others' judgment of her own mind until it is too late.
characters.backStory: Recently gave birth; her writing and independence have been curtailed by the prescribed rest.

characters.name: John
characters.characterSketch: The narrator's husband, a practical physician who is certain there is nothing seriously wrong with her.
characters.appearance: Composed and authoritative; the picture of professional confidence.
characters.physNotes: Healthy, brisk, frequently away on cases.
characters.psychNotes: Rational to a fault; mistakes control for care.
characters.flaw: Cannot believe a condition he cannot measure.
characters.backStory: A respected doctor who prescribes his own wife the fashionable rest cure.

settings.name: The Nursery
settings.summary: A large upstairs room with barred windows and peeling yellow wallpaper, once a nursery, where the narrator is kept to rest.
settings.locale: A colonial mansion let for the summer, set well back from the road
settings.lighting: Changeable daylight through barred windows; moonlight at night
settings.sights: Sprawling, lurid yellow wallpaper with a confused, repeating pattern
settings.sounds: Quiet of an isolated house; the narrator's own restless movement
settings.smellTaste: A peculiar lingering smell the narrator attributes to the paper

scenes.name: The narrator studies the wallpaper
scenes.description: Left alone in the nursery, the narrator traces the wallpaper's pattern and becomes convinced there is a figure trapped behind it. John, when present, insists she is improving and must not give in to fancy.
scenes.protGoal: Make sense of the room and her own worsening state
scenes.antagGoal: Suppress her perceptions and submit to the rest cure
scenes.outcome: The narrator sinks further into obsession with the paper.

problems.name: The narrator's mental decline
problems.storyQuestion: Will the narrator hold onto her sanity under the rest cure?
problems.problemSource: Protagonist is placed in strange surroundings
problems.protGoal: To recover and be believed about her own mind
problems.antagGoal: To submit to the rest cure and silence her own perceptions
problems.antagMotive: Fear, isolation, and the weight of others' certainty
problems.outcome: The narrator loses her grip on reality, freeing the woman she sees in the paper.
